identity.name: Agnimanth
historical_botanical_names: Clerodendron phlomidis Linn. (older treatment/name shown in textbook)
identity.taxonomy_note: Premna integrifolia L. is the historical/medicinal-source name used in the record; Kew Plants of the World Online currently treats it as a synonym of Premna serratifolia L. The genus Premna is currently placed in Lamiaceae. Historical Ayurvedic and pharmacognostic literature may use Verbenaceae or Clerodendrum names.
identity.family_note: Lamiaceae (current Kew placement); older literature may list Verbenaceae.

classification.habit: Large shrub or small tree, reaching about 9 m in height.
classification.habitat: Reported throughout India; abundant in Karnataka and Maharashtra and in drier parts. Classical synonyms also describe growth on river banks.
classification.distribution: India; textbook notes abundant occurrence in Karnataka and Maharashtra and throughout drier parts.

identification.description: Large shrub or small tree with woody, branched habit. The supplied textbook records yellowish, lenticellate bark; simple broadly elliptic leaves; terminal pubescent paniculate corymbose cymes; small greenish-yellow flowers with disagreeable odour; and small pear-shaped fruits.
identification.whole_plant: Large shrub or small tree, up to about 9 m high, with branched woody habit.
identification.root: Cylindrical to somewhat twisted/knarled roots, sometimes longitudinally split, gradually tapering. Surface rough or longitudinally fissured and yellowish-brown; debarked surface may be silky yellow and longitudinally striated. Transverse section shows bark, narrow cortex, woody region with concentric rings and a small central pith.
identification.stem: Woody, branched; mature bark described as yellowish and lenticellate; trunk and large branches may be spinous.
identification.leaf: Leaves 5–9 cm long × 3–6 cm wide, broadly elliptic, obtuse, very shortly acuminate, glabrous, entire or dentate in the upper part, base rounded or subacute, with 4–5 pairs of main nerves; petiole about 1 cm.
identification.flower: Small, greenish-yellow flowers with disagreeable odour; borne in terminal pubescent paniculate corymbose cymes.
identification.fruit: Small pear-shaped fruit, about 4 mm long.
identification.seed: Seed characters are not detailed on the supplied pages.
identification.bark: Yellowish, lenticellate bark; trunk and large branches sometimes spinous.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The supplied textbook research section lists premnine as an alkaloid and reports additional root/stem-bark/leaf constituents. Constituent names and spelling should be cross-checked with the cited primary literature before treating the list as an analytical profile.

modern_information.evidence_summary: The supplied textbook research section reports experimental studies involving Clerodendrum phlomidis, including hypoglycaemic activity of leaf aqueous extract, anthelmintic activity, anti-inflammatory/antiarthritic activity, hepatoprotective findings in CCl4-induced liver injury models, analgesic activity of aerial-part extracts, and in-vitro antioxidant assays. These are preclinical/experimental findings and should not be interpreted as proof of clinical efficacy.

diagnostic_characters.shape: Cylindrical, knarled roots or longitudinally split pieces.
diagnostic_characters.surface: Rough, longitudinally wrinkled, yellowish-brown with small round root scars; debarked surface silky yellow and longitudinally striated; transverse section shows closely adhering thin bark, narrow cortex, large woody portion with prominent concentric rings and small central pith.

diagnostic_characters.shape: Cylindrical, somewhat twisted, gradually tapering roots, up to about 3 cm in diameter.
diagnostic_characters.surface: Longitudinally fissured, yellowish-brown; transverse cut portion creamish-yellow; thin bark easily separates; well-defined annual rings and dark-brown central pith. Bark occurs as small flat/slightly curved friable pieces about 1.5–2 mm thick with brown exfoliating inner surface.

basonym: अग्निं मथ्नाति दीप्नत्वात् — the supplied text explains the name in relation to the fire-producing property of rubbing dried sticks and its digestive-fire stimulating association.

research_corner: Experimental hypoglycaemic activity is reported for aqueous leaf extract.
Studies of Clerodendrum phlomidis extracts reported hepatoprotective findings in CCl4-induced liver injury models.
Aerial-part extracts were evaluated for analgesic activity; methanolic and ethyl-acetate fractions were reported active at 200 mg/kg in the cited study.
Methanolic root extract was reported to show in-vitro antioxidant activity in radical-scavenging and lipid-peroxidation assays.
Crude ethanolic extract was evaluated in anti-inflammatory and adjuvant-induced antiarthritic experimental models.
